No component of the evidence model changes val accuracy measurably (Table~\ref{tab:ablations}):
each ablation moves seed-42 F1 by at most \ablMaxAbsDeltaFOne{} points (smallest $p\ablMinPFOne$).
Ranking is just as flat: model-mined, lexical, random and no negatives reach the same Recall@1,
so mining the ranker's own hardest sentence does not beat BM25-selected negatives, and the audit
in \S\ref{sec:evidence-labels} finds the two equally often plausible. The full model beats BM25 by
\ablRoneDeltaROneAbs{} Recall@1 points ($p\ablRonePROne$), yet the span-only model's implied ranking
is as good (R3: \ablRthreeDeltaROne{}, $p\ablRthreePROne$): the reader already finds the answer
sentence. Joint decoding matters least: $\lambda=0$ (R7) changes \ablRsevenChangedAnswers{} of
\ablNQuestions{} answers, and the best $\lambda$ gains at most \lamMaxGain{} F1
(Figure~\ref{fig:lambda}).
